The paper introduces heuristic offline classification techniques for handwritten signatures based on boundary tracing.
Signature images are converted to binary maps using thresholding to remove minor distortions.
Outer and inner boundaries of signatures are treated separately and divided into upper and lower parts for feature extraction.
Three feature vector extraction methods are proposed: y-coordinate sequences, vectors between consecutive points, and polar coordinate vectors.
Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) with window and slope constraints is used for classification.
A dataset of 60 signatures from 20 individuals (3 signatures each) was used for experiments.
Classification accuracy reached up to 93% when including internal loop information with a weighting factor of 4.
The view-based approach achieved classification accuracies between 74.17% and 84.17% depending on DTW variant and window size.
Sampling every 10th point was used to reduce feature vector size and remove noise effects.
The Manhattan distance was used as the distance metric in DTW computations.
Incorporating the number of internal loops in signatures improved classification results.
The slope constraint in DTW restricts warping paths to certain directions to avoid singularities.
Boundary tracing methods outperform view-based methods in classification accuracy but are computationally more expensive.
The authors plan to combine offline signature features with online data from cameras or tablets for hybrid recognition systems.
Future work includes applying neural networks, Hidden Markov Models, and Toeplitz matrix eigenvalue analysis for feature extraction.
The paper compares the proposed methods with previous works, showing improved classification rates.
The paper was published in 2006 in the International Scientific Journal of Computing.
The authors are affiliated with Bialystok Technical University, Poland.
The classification process treats signatures as whole words without segmenting into letters or strokes.
The DTW algorithm is adapted with window and slope constraints to improve alignment accuracy.
